scope_notes: The full black-box interface is proved only for k = 1.
The unmodified projection convergence is proved for every k > 0.
The actual normalized first compression moment converges almost surely, on one event for all real coefficient vectors.

The actual normalized second compression moment converges almost surely for each fixed real coefficient vector, with k >= 2 and t in [0,1], via an exact fourth-order Haar variance calculation and Borel-Cantelli.
Conditional reduction theorems retain their displayed hypotheses.
All finite Haar projection entry products and compression trace moments are evaluated at every order up to the ambient dimension, including k >= 2 and signed coefficient vectors.
The invariant tensor spanning theorem, Gram invertibility, Haar integration formula, and cycle contractions are proved rather than assumed.
Exact normalized Gram and quantitative inverse-Gram row estimates are proved with the product error parameter.
These finite formulas do not yet establish higher-order limiting freeness or sharp spectral outlier exclusion.
Arbitrary-order finite Neumann approximations to the normalized inverse Gram matrix have vanishing error after any fixed polynomial dimension amplification.
The inverse-Gram estimates are transferred to the actual canonical expected compression trace at every fixed order, giving a finite inverse-free expression with vanishing absolute error.
All fourth-order permutation certificates are checked by the kernel with decide; no native-decide oracle is used.
The deterministic signed spectral interval is a common support enclosure, not a sharp limiting support or outlier-exclusion theorem.
remaining_obligations: Evaluate the finite Neumann/permutation expressions to identify all limiting moments with the Bernoulli free-sum law, and prove summable fluctuation control beyond the first and second moments.
Sharp upper spectral bounds excluding outliers for general block compressions.
Assembly of FullBlockModifiedStrongInput for every required k and t.
